title: Hypercontractive bounds for unit atoms
statement: Let $P$ be a finite product probability space with coordinate atom weights at least $1$, and let $q>2$, $ho\in\mathbb R$, and $f$ be a real-valued function on its product outcome space. Then the product noise operator satisfies both $\|T_\rho f\|_{q,P}\le \|f\|_{2,P}$ and $\|T_\rho f\|_{2,P}\le \|f\|_{q/(q-1),P}$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite product probability space with strictly positive coordinate weights summing to one
Every coordinate atom has weight at least $1$
$f$ is a real-valued function on the product outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ with every coordinate atom at least $1$, and let $q>2$ and $\rho\in\mathbb R$. For every $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, $\|T_\rho f\|_{q,P}\le\|f\|_{2,P}$ and $\|T_\rho f\|_{2,P}\le\|f\|_{q/(q-1),P}$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $T_a h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a^{|S|}h_S$ for every real rate $a$; $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$. The powers indexed by subset cardinalities are natural powers, including $0^0=1$.
